description:
Goal
Preserve the correct runtime shape for closure captures on the quicksort native path so a value that should be a closure capture never degrades into an atom/scalar lane.

Problem being fixed
The widened native-program suite still fails on quicksort after fz-hwn.6. The crash is not test drift and not the old omitted-lane bug. Runtime executes a closure capture load and finds an atom where a closure is expected.

Verified failure
- `cargo test compiler2_native_program_jit_runs_quicksort_through_compiler2_codegen --lib -- --nocapture`
- Runtime panic: `fz_closure_get_capture_i64 closure: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(4), found: ValueKind(0) }`

What we know
- Backend/interpreter quicksort is green, so the earlier runtime-demand / artifact transport work is not the current root.
- The failure happens on the native path after codegen, which means some native/codegen seam is still flattening or mis-materializing a closure capture into the wrong runtime shape.
- The fix should trace the first place the capture stops being represented as the demanded callable/runtime value and becomes a scalar/atom instead.

Design rule
- Closure captures must keep the runtime shape chosen by settled layout all the way through native lowering and codegen.
- A capture that is semantically callable may only become a scalar lane if settled layout explicitly says so.
- Do not patch the runtime to tolerate the wrong shape; fix the compiler seam where the shape becomes wrong.

Code seams
- quicksort native lowering and codegen path
- closure capture encoding/materialization helpers
- any continuation/delivered-return path that rebinds quicksort captures

Checks
- `cargo test compiler2_native_program_jit_runs_quicksort_through_compiler2_codegen --lib`
- no `fz_closure_get_capture_i64` runtime panic
- quicksort still keeps tuple-field return/input demand explicit where already proven
title: Compiler2 native quicksort loses closure capture runtime shape
